cards.name: fix-the-timing-unit-before-the-lever-when-the-weight-stream-rivals-the-last-level-cache
cards.description: Hot or per-kernel-isolated timing inverts cache and layout levers when the weight stream rivals last-level cache: only flushed whole-cluster A/B is admissible.
cards.key: choosing the timing unit for a fused producer-consumer dispatch pair on gfx950 whose streamed weight set is a large fraction of the last-level cache, where residency state rather than the candidate decides the number
cards.title: Fix the timing unit before the lever when the weight stream rivals the last-level cache
cards.effect: two independent levers each inverted sign between residency states, non-overlapping in both, on the decode case: a non-temporal hint removed from the streamed weight operand read 1.33x hot and 0.73x cold, and a weight preshuffle read 1.32-1.38x hot and 0.745x cold (0.86x cold on the prefill case). A third, a non-temporal hint on the epilogue read of the producer's output, was faster measured per-kernel-isolated and slower measured in-cluster on both cases (~1.02x once removed in-cluster at prefill). Against a baseline self-speedup spread of about +/-1.5% measured on the unmodified body, the run's best director-verified candidate was +0.035%, roughly a fortieth of that band
cards.roofline: memory-bound both sides; the streamed weight set is about 0.7 of last-level cache capacity, so an unflushed loop measures a resident operand. Cold, the decode arm reaches ~0.35 of nameplate stream rate against ~0.43 read under uncontrolled timing, and both weighted cases sit within ~1.1x of their own backend-family ceilings
cards.lever: Before funding any direction on a fused producer-consumer pair, settle the timing unit: time the whole cluster as one unit, with the cache flushed, under graph replay, and re-measure the incumbent yourself under that protocol instead of inheriting a stored best time. Publish the unmodified body's self-speedup spread under the same protocol first, and treat that band as the admissibility bar for every candidate.
cards.apply: One timing entry point that captures producer plus consumer in a single graph and flushes between reps; capture the candidate configs up front and sample them round-robin, one rep at a time, rather than running each config as a block; carry an unmodified arm through the same rotation every round.
cards.verify: Confirm every arm keeps its sign under both framings before believing it: measured per-kernel-isolated and measured inside the cluster, and hot versus flushed. An arm whose sign moves is reporting residency, not the candidate. A candidate inside the published self-speedup band is not a result even when the correctness gate passes.
cards.pitfall:
A cache-modifier removal on the streamed weight operand read a large win in an unflushed back-to-back loop and survived a full harness run with a passing weighted-speedup number and a correctness pass -> the weight set is a large fraction of last-level cache, so the loop was timing a resident operand -> re-time every arm flushed under graph replay before any harness number is quoted.
A non-temporal hint on the epilogue's read of the producer's output was faster isolated and slower in-cluster -> in isolation the producer's output has been evicted so the read really is a cold stream, while in-cluster it is still resident and the hint discards exactly that residency -> for a fused pair, time the cluster; a per-kernel-in-isolation number can invert.
A config sweep produced apparent 1.05-1.10x readings that vanished on repeat -> configs were benched in sequential blocks and the dominant GEMM drifts several percent across blocks -> capture the configs up front and interleave them sample-by-sample.
A vendor tuner's stored best entry for the incumbent sat about 20% below anything reproducible cold, and a whole direction was sized against that gap -> the stored entry is a hot measurement -> re-measure the incumbent cold before treating a tuning table as headroom.
cards.caution: Also verify the working-set-to-cache ratio before trusting any prior number on the kernel, including your own from an earlier round: at about 0.7 of capacity the hot-versus-cold gap here was larger than every real effect the run measured, and one earlier round's rationale had to be revised once its isolated measurement was redone in-cluster.
cards.source: run k1_gemm_actmul_fusion_task-qwen3-14b-fp8-lane, 2026-09-09, gfx950/MI355X, rounds 1-2 (5 directions, 0 banked, workspace byte-identical to the frozen baseline); director-validated 1.000x weighted
